AI engineering in practice
AI engineering is moving faster than the playbook.

Teams are making decisions about agents, context, evaluation, security, permissions, and production reliability
while many of the practices are still changing.

Finding another article or demo is rarely the hard part. The harder part is deciding what applies to your system,
what changes under your constraints, and what you should do next.

The cohorts give that process a structure. You examine the work with experienced practitioners from other
organizations, see how the same decisions change in different environments, and put the thinking into practice
between sessions.

How the five weeks work.

Selected QCon and InfoQ material provides a starting point. The live sessions are where participants examine the
approach, challenge assumptions, and hear how the same decision changes in other environments.

Between sessions, participants put the thinking into practice in work they already own. The next session builds
on what happened.

5 weeks
One cohort, start to finish

4 live hours
Each week

Time-boxed
Work between sessions

Capstone
In week five

See upcoming dates

Before
Before each week’s live work, use selected QCon material as the starting point.

During
During the sessions, work through the technical problem with the facilitator and cohort.

Between
Between sessions, apply the material to your own system or workflow.

Back in session
Return with the result and discuss where the approach changed under your constraints.

Week five
The final week includes the capstone.

Different operating contexts
Compare your assumptions with people working elsewhere.

Your experience is shaped by the systems and organizations you have worked in. The cohort puts your reasoning
alongside experienced practitioners dealing with different architecture, scale, regulation, incentives, and team
structures.

The useful comparison is where an approach transfers, where it changes, and why. You still own the decision and what
happens next in your environment.

The capstone
Finish with work you can point to.

Each AI program ends with a program-specific capstone based on the work covered across the five weeks.

The exact artifact depends on the program. The current capstone requirements are shown on each cohort page.

The programs are designed for experienced practitioners, generally with at least five years of professional
experience.

The technical material and practitioner network come from InfoQ and QCon.

A QCon talk or InfoQ article can introduce a practitioner's approach. In these cohorts, one practitioner stays
with the same group for five weeks while participants apply the material to their own systems, teams, and
constraints.

AI topic FAQ

Which AI program should I choose?

+
−

Choose based on the decisions you are responsible for.

AI Engineering
Building and operating production AI systems.

AI Security & Privacy Engineering
Sensitive data, threats, controls, evaluation, governance, and auditing.

AI-Assisted Engineering
The engineering environment around coding agents, including context, permissions, review, and unattended workflows.

Are these introductory AI courses?

+
−

No. The programs are designed for experienced software practitioners already responsible for technical decisions in the area.

Why a cohort instead of self-paced material?

+
−

The material is only the starting point. The cohort gives you recurring time to examine it with people working under different constraints, put it into practice, and return with what happened.

Are the sessions recorded?

+
−

No. The live sessions are not recorded so participants can discuss current systems and organizational context more openly.

Can I get help making the case internally?

+
−

Yes. Use the Convince Your Manager page to copy a guided AI prompt or start from a ready-to-edit email template. Choose the cohort you are considering so the current dates, price, facilitator, time commitment, and capstone are included.

Build the manager case

Do the cohorts follow the same syllabus?

+
−

Each program has a core syllabus. When a different facilitator leads a cohort, parts of the program may be adapted around that facilitator’s experience and the needs of the group. Where a cohort has a specific emphasis, it is stated on the cohort card and cohort page.

Do all AI programs lead to an InfoQ certification?

+
−

Yes, where the current program terms state certification is awarded after the participation and capstone requirements are met.
